absent: Values and allocation algorithms for legacy and top down bases, randomness widths, task size limits, default window boundary, and orientation flag semantics.
Layouts of address space descriptor, limit structure, register file, probe descriptor, trace record, prefix attribute bundle, and access classification enumeration.
Contents of opcode and prefix tables, register identifier enumeration, high byte aliasing rules, and full width mapping beyond summarized categories.
Semantics of address translation, probe lifecycle, trace emission, enabled state query, CPU hotplug operations, read locking, and grace period handling.

NUMA platform discovery, emulation command handling, table disable controls, early accessor behavior, identifier limits, node mask iteration, memblock coverage, frame range query, node data allocation, and device tree interaction.
Lock ordering across mutex and spinlock, interrupt state expectations, per CPU access rules, and memory ordering guarantees.
Recovery beyond fatal aborts, multiprocessor event ordering, filter offset application, and mapping identity allocation.

findings.text: Provides address space setup that records legacy versus top down orientation and stores randomized mapping origins for native and compat execution contexts, plus a current task accessor that selects among stored origins using legacy request and syscall width.

A user hint is accepted only when its extent remains inside overall task range and stays on one side of the default window edge. Physical range checks accept only extents fully contained within directly mapped memory or reported valid by the physical address validator.

Modification permission defaults to allow and only narrows on machines flagged vulnerable to a speculative leak when protection encoding requests inversion for non present frame numbers at or beyond a platform limit without administrative privilege.

Fault context pairs probed location with faulting instruction location together with access classification and per CPU nesting depth. Remap tracking links list linkage with probe descriptor plus originating physical base and numeric mapping identity.

Per CPU fault and trace records avoid cross CPU sharing. A mutex serializes tracer start stop and list mutation. An interrupt safe spinlock guards event emission. An atomic counter represents enabled state checked by helpers.

Module scope controls provide an address filter offset, a hard disable switch that skips probe registration, and a toggle for capturing program counter values versus zeroing them for clean room use. Diagnostic output shares a common textual prefix.
Page table diagnostic reports missing entries and aborts execution when encountering an unsupported large page size, so tracing unexpected mappings can terminate the machine rather than recover.

Tracing enforces at most one active fault per CPU. Entry classifies the faulting instruction and snapshots physical location mapping identity width and value, with program counter capture conditional. Exit finalizes read values and emits the record, restoring idle depth. Any reentry or unbalanced completion is treated as fatal.

Instruction classifier reports whether the bytes at a given location encode a register read, register write, immediate write, or unrelated operation by skipping prefixes decoding the opcode and consulting operation tables.

Prefix scanning consumes legacy override bytes and records operand size reduction plus address size and extension attributes including REX presence. Opcode decoding handles single byte forms and two byte extended forms introduced by an escape byte.

Width helpers map decoded operation to byte, word, double word, or quad word sizes, adjusting for operand size override and address extension attributes, and report zero with diagnostic on unknown operation.

Value extraction returns the current content of the referenced general register sized by decoded width, using a fixed accumulator for string store forms and ModR/M register selection otherwise, or locates trailing immediate bytes after accounting for displacement determined by addressing mode.

Formatted trace output acquires interrupt safe exclusion and emits only while enabled. List purge assumes exclusive mutex ownership with tracing disabled and stable, unregistering probes then freeing entries after a grace period.

Enable initializes low level probes, reduces to single CPU where supported, then marks tracing active. Disable clears active marking, purges pending remaps with guarantee of no further callbacks, restores CPUs, and tears down probes. Both paths are serialized and idempotent against repeated requests.

One build implements CPU reduction by allocating a mask, snapshotting online set minus first CPU, and offlining each listed processor with per CPU diagnostics, restoring them on exit. An alternate build without hotplug support performs no reduction and only warns when multiple CPUs remain online.
Early boot option parsing records NUMA disable requests and dispatches emulation, ACPI table, and heterogeneity table controls to dedicated handlers, rejecting missing option text.

APIC identifier to node mapping is sized by maximum local APIC count with all entries defaulting to no node. Node to CPU mask storage is sized by maximum node count. Coverage validation uses one megabyte granularity.
CPU to node resolution consults early APIC identifier storage and falls back to no node for invalid identifiers. Physical node counting measures weight of parsed node mask.
CPU node assignment writes through early firmware mapping storage when present, otherwise updates per CPU mapping and topology state, with clearing defined as assignment to no node.

Boot initialization ensures node identifier range is established, allocates per node CPU masks, then validates memblock coverage and brings online only nodes that span a non empty frame interval while instantiating node data.

NUMA bring up resets APIC to node state, builds memory blocks top down, registers nodes, prunes CPUs bound to offline nodes, and round robins remaining unassigned CPUs across online nodes. Top level selection prefers ACPI, then platform specific, then device tree when ACPI is disabled, finally falling back to a single fake node covering all memory with appropriate diagnostics.

Late initialization promotes generic initiator nodes and CPU associated nodes to online to avoid ordering constraints with node registration during secondary CPU bring up, requiring early APIC storage to be present.

Tracing timestamps are recorded after handling rather than at fault time, leaving multiprocessor ordering uncertain, and remaining online secondary CPUs risk missed events. Node promotion relies on early mapping tables whose absence is fatal.

Decoder treats 0x66 as operand size override, 0x40 family as extension prefixes, 0x0F as extended opcode escape, and 0xAA with 0xAB as fixed string stores. Displacement after ModR/M is one or four bytes depending on addressing mode, with register selection from middle bits and mode from top bits.
